tools.name: box_agent_run
tools.description: Run an AI agent prompt inside an Upstash Box. The agent has access to shell, filesystem, and git inside the box. It reasons, executes commands, and iterates until the task is complete. This is a synchronous call that may take a while depending on the complexity of the prompt.

box_id.description: The box ID to run the agent in

prompt.description: The natural-language prompt for the agent to execute

model.description: Override the box's default LLM model for this run

folder.description: Working directory inside the box for the agent

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_exec
tools.description: Execute a shell command inside an Upstash Box container. Use this for file operations, git commands, package installs, or any shell operation inside the box.

box_id.description: The box ID to execute the command in

command.description: Command and arguments as an array (e.g. ['bash', '-c', 'ls -la'])

async.description: If true, return immediately without waiting for completion

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_logs
tools.description: Get logs from an Upstash Box container. Useful for debugging what happened inside the box. Returns timestamped log entries from the system, user, and agent sources.

box_id.description: The box ID to get logs for

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (max 1000, default: 100)

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_manage
tools.description: Manage Upstash Box containers. Supports creating, listing, getting, deleting, pausing, resuming, and forking boxes. Boxes are secure cloud containers with built-in AI agent capabilities.

box_id.description: Box ID (required for get, delete, pause, resume, fork)

model.description: LLM model to use (e.g. 'claude/sonnet_4_6', 'openai/o4-mini'). Required for create

agent_api_key.description: API key for the AI agent provider. Empty uses managed key

env_vars.description: Environment variables to set in the box

clone_repo.description: Git repository URL to clone into the box

ephemeral.description: If true, box auto-deletes after TTL expires

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds for ephemeral boxes (max 259200 = 3 days)

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_preview
tools.description: Manage preview URLs for web applications running inside an Upstash Box. Create public URLs to access services running on specific ports, list existing previews, or delete them.

port.description: Port number (required for create and delete)

basic_auth.description: Enable basic auth on the preview URL (create only)

bearer_token.description: Enable bearer token auth on the preview URL (create only)

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_runs
tools.description: List, get details, or cancel runs (execution history) for an Upstash Box. Useful for debugging past agent runs and shell executions, checking their status, output, token usage, and costs.

run_id.description: Run ID (required for get and cancel actions)

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: box_snapshots
tools.description: Manage Upstash Box snapshots. Create full filesystem snapshots of a box, list snapshots, delete them, or restore a box from a snapshot.

action.description: The action to perform. 'list' lists snapshots for a specific box, 'list_all' lists all your snapshots

box_id.description: Box ID (required for create, list, delete)

snapshot_id.description: Snapshot ID (required for delete and restore)

name.description: Name for the snapshot (auto-generated if empty)

model.description: LLM model for the restored box (required for restore)

runtime.description: Override the snapshot's runtime for the restored box

env_vars.description: Environment variables for the restored box

ephemeral.description: Create the restored box as ephemeral

ttl.description: TTL in seconds for the restored ephemeral box (max 259200)

box_api_key.description: Box API key (starts with 'box_'). Check the project's .env file for BOX_API_KEY, or ask the user for it.

tools.name: qstash_publish_message
tools.description:
Publish a message to a destination URL using QStash. This
    sends an HTTP request to the specified destination via QStash's message
    queue. This can also be used to trigger a upstash workflow run.

destination.description: The destination URL to send the message to (e.g., 'https://example.com')

body.description: Request body (JSON string or plain text)

retries.description: Number of retries on failure, default is 3

callback.description: Callback URL that will be called when the message is successfully delivered

failureCallback.description: Callback URL that will be called when the message is failed to deliver

queueName.description: Queue name to use, you have to first create the queue in upstash. Prefer the flow control key instead

key.description: Unique identifier for grouping messages under same flow control rules

period.description: Time window for rate limit (e.g., '1s', '1m', '1h', default: '1s')

flow_control.description: Flow control for rate limiting and parallelism management

extraHeaders.description: Extra headers to add to the request

region.description: QStash region to use. To use local mode, pick `local`

local_mode_port.description: Only provide when using local mode and if default does not work, the port is usually in the .env file

tools.name: redis_database_create_new
tools.description:
Create a new Upstash redis database. 
NOTE: Ask user for the region and name of the database.
NOTE: Don't show the database ID from the response to the user unless explicitly asked or needed.

primary_region.description: Primary Region of the Global Database.

read_regions.description: Array of read regions of the db

tools.name: redis_database_delete
tools.description: Delete an Upstash redis database.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to delete.

tools.name: redis_database_get_details
tools.description:
Get further details of a specific Upstash redis database. Includes all details of the database including usage statistics.
db_disk_threshold: Total disk usage limit.
db_memory_threshold: Maximum memory usage.
db_daily_bandwidth_limit: Maximum daily network bandwidth usage.
db_request_limit: Total number of commands allowed.
All sizes are in bytes

NOTE: Don't show the database ID from the response to the user unless explicitly asked or needed.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to get details for.

tools.name: redis_database_get_statistics
tools.description:
Get comprehensive usage statistics of an Upstash redis database. Returns both:
1. PRECISE 5-day usage: Exact command count and bandwidth usage over the last 5 days
2. SAMPLED period stats: Sampled statistics over a specified period (1h, 3h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 7d) for performance monitoring

For sampled stats, includes: read_latency_mean, write_latency_mean, keyspace, throughput (cmds/sec), diskusage
NOTE: If user doesn't specify stat_type, defaults to "throughput" for sampled stats.
NOTE: Ask user first if they want to see stats for each database separately or just for one.

anyOf.description: commands per second (sampled), calculate area for estimated count

stat_type.description: The type of sampled stat to get (defaults to 'throughput')

tools.name: redis_database_list_backups
tools.description: List all backups of a specific Upstash redis database.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to list backups for.

tools.name: redis_database_list_databases
tools.description:
List all Upstash redis databases. Only their names and ids.
NOTE: Don't show the database ID from the response to the user unless explicitly asked or needed.

tools.name: redis_database_manage_backup
tools.description: Create, delete, or restore backups for a specific Upstash redis database. This tool handles all backup operations in one unified interface.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to manage backups for.

operation.description: The backup operation to perform: create, delete, or restore.

backup_name.description: Name for the backup (required for create operation).

backup_id.description: ID of the backup (required for delete and restore operations).

tools.name: redis_database_reset_password
tools.description: Reset the password of an Upstash redis database.

tools.name: redis_database_run_redis_commands
tools.description:
Run one or more Redis commands on a specific Upstash redis database. Either provide database_id OR both database_rest_url and database_rest_token.
NOTE: For discovery, use SCAN over KEYS. Use TYPE to get the type of a key.
NOTE: SCAN cursor [MATCH pattern] [COUNT count] [TYPE type]
NOTE: Multiple commands will be executed as a pipeline for better performance.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to run commands on.

database_rest_url.description: The REST URL of the database. Example: https://***.upstash.io

database_rest_token.description: The REST token of the database.

commands.description: The Redis commands to run. For single command: [['SET', 'foo', 'bar']], for multiple: [['SET', 'foo', 'bar'], ['GET', 'foo']]

tools.name: redis_database_set_daily_backup
tools.description: Enable or disable daily backups for a specific Upstash redis database.

database_id.description: The ID of the database to enable or disable daily backups for.

enable.description: Whether to enable or disable daily backups.

tools.name: redis_database_update_regions
tools.description: Update the read regions of an Upstash redis database.

read_regions.description: Array of the new read regions of the database. This will replace the old regions array. Available regions: us-east-1, us-west-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, sa-east-1
